also: vendor's live database
live monitors tool
Monitoring tools that watch activity as it happens and can flag suspicious behavior immediately.
also: real-time monitoring
Live Patch product
A Check Point service that automatically applies certain protections or fixes without a full manual update.
Llama product
Llama is a family of large language models released by Meta that can generate and analyze text.
Llama Guard 3 product
A family of AI safety models designed to classify whether text is allowed or unsafe.
llama-guard3:8b product
An approximately eight-billion-parameter Llama Guard model used to classify whether AI content is safe.
also: llama-guard3
LLM concept
An LLM, or large language model, is an AI system trained on large amounts of text to understand and generate language.
also: large language model, agentic LLM’s, model, modern AI models
LLM Steganography technique
The practice of hiding instructions or data inside apparently harmless content intended for a large language model.
LLMjacking technique
LLMjacking is the abuse of someone else’s AI or cloud account to run large language model workloads at their expense.
LLMs concept
LLMs are large language models, which are AI systems trained on lots of text so they can generate and understand language.
local privilege escalation technique
A technique where an attacker with limited system access exploits a flaw to gain higher administrative rights.
also: Windows privilege elevation flaw, LPE
Local Session Manager product
A Windows component that manages user logons, logoffs, and local or remote sessions.
lock-screen overlays technique
A technique in which an app displays content over a device's lock screen, potentially blocking access or deceiving the user.
Lock-Screen PINs concept
Short number codes used to unlock a phone or other device.
Log4Shell vulnerability
Log4Shell is the widely exploited Log4j vulnerability that allowed remote code execution in many Java applications.
logging concept
Logging is the recording of events and actions so people can review what happened later.
Login information concept
Login information is data such as usernames, passwords, codes, or tokens used to access an account.
logistics concept
Logistics is the planning and movement of goods, people, or resources from one place to another.
logistics provider organization
A logistics provider is a company that helps move, store, or deliver goods for other businesses.
Longtale threat-actor
A threat-actor group referenced in security reporting.
Longtale/GemStone credential stealer extension malware
A malicious browser extension designed to steal passwords, session data, and other account information.
Low-privileged account concept
A low-privileged account is a user account with limited permissions, reducing what it can access or change.
LSASS memory dumping technique
A technique that extracts data from the Windows LSASS process, which can contain account passwords and login credentials.
Lumma Stealer malware
Lumma Stealer is malware that steals passwords, browser cookies, cryptocurrency wallets, and other sensitive data.
lure technique
A lure is bait used by attackers, such as a fake offer or message, to persuade someone to click or act.
lures technique
Lures are messages, files, or themes attackers use to tempt people into clicking a link, opening an attachment, or taking another risky action.
macOS product
macOS is Apple’s operating system for Mac computers.
macOS product
Apple's desktop operating system for Mac computers.
Macs product
Macs are Apple personal computers that can be targets or managed endpoints in security operations.
also: managed devices
Magento product
Magento is an e-commerce platform used to build and run online stores, now associated with Adobe Commerce.
Magento Open Source product
Magento Open Source is a free, open-source e-commerce platform now associated with Adobe Commerce.
Mailbox concept
A mailbox is the storage location where a person's email messages are received and kept.
Mailboxes concept
Mailboxes are email accounts or storage locations where messages are received and kept.
Maintainers concept
Maintainers are the people responsible for updating, reviewing, and managing a software project.
Malicious concept
Malicious means intentionally harmful, such as software or behavior designed to damage, steal, or deceive.
malicious activity concept
Malicious activity is any harmful or unauthorized action, such as stealing data, spreading malware, or breaking into systems.
Malicious APKs technique
Harmful Android app installation files that can install malware on a device.
Malicious Browser Extensions malware
Browser add-ons designed to steal data, alter browsing, or perform other harmful actions.
malicious code concept
Malicious code is software instructions written to harm systems, steal data, or give attackers control.
Malicious content concept
Malicious content is any file, link, code, or message designed to harm users or systems.
malicious link concept
A malicious link is a web link designed to lead someone to malware, scams, fake login pages, or other harmful content.
malicious package malware
A malicious package is a software package that contains harmful code or was created to trick users into installing it.
malicious packages malware
Malicious packages are software libraries published or shared with harmful code hidden inside them.
malware concept
Malware is software made to harm, spy on, or take control of computers or data.
malware analysis technique
Malware analysis is the study of malicious software to understand what it does and how to detect or stop it.
malware loader malware
A malware loader is malicious software that installs or launches other malware on a victim's device.
Man-in-the-Middle technique
A Man-in-the-Middle attack happens when an attacker secretly intercepts or alters communication between two parties.
Management system product
A management system is software used to configure, monitor, and control devices, users, or services.
Mantax Otax malware
A mobile malware family that combines device spying capabilities with ransomware-like behavior.
master key concept
A master key is a main secret key that can unlock or protect other keys, passwords, or encrypted data.

MCP, or Model Context Protocol, is a standard way for AI assistants to connect to external tools, files, and services.

An MCP Server is a server that implements the Model Context Protocol to connect AI systems with tools, data, or services.
MCP tools tool
MCP tools are capabilities exposed through the Model Context Protocol so an AI system can call external functions or services.
MediaProjection API protocol
An Android programming interface that allows an app, with permission, to capture screen content or record the display.
medical cards concept
Medical cards are documents or cards used to show healthcare coverage, benefits, or medical identity information.
memory corruption vulnerability vulnerability
A memory corruption vulnerability is a software flaw where memory is handled incorrectly, potentially causing crashes or allowing attackers to run code.
memory-corruption flaw vulnerability
A memory-corruption flaw is a software bug where a program mishandles memory, sometimes letting attackers crash it or run code.
memory-resident technique
Memory-resident means software runs mainly in a computer’s temporary memory rather than being stored as an obvious file on disk.
Mentions concept
References to a person or organization found in monitored sources such as websites or news.
Meta organization
The parent company of Facebook, Instagram, and WhatsApp, a major player in social media and ad-tech.
Metabase product
Metabase is an open-source business intelligence tool used to query databases and build dashboards.
Metadata concept
Metadata is data that describes other data, such as when a file was created, who sent an email, or where a photo was taken.
METR organization
METR, the Model Evaluation and Threat Research organization, studies and evaluates risks from advanced AI systems.
mexico
Mexico is a North American country that may appear in cybersecurity reporting as a location, target, or government context.
MFA concept
MFA is the shortened name for multi-factor authentication, a login process that uses more than one proof of identity.
MFA fatigue technique
MFA fatigue is an attack where criminals repeatedly send login approval prompts until a tired or confused user accepts one.
MI6 organization
MI6 is the common name for the United Kingdom's Secret Intelligence Service, which gathers foreign intelligence.
microcontroller product
A microcontroller is a tiny computer chip that controls functions inside devices.
microsoft organization
Microsoft is a major technology company that makes Windows, Office, Azure, and many enterprise security products.
Microsoft Configuration Manager product
Microsoft Configuration Manager is a Microsoft product used to manage, update, and deploy software to many Windows devices.
Microsoft Defender product
Microsoft Defender is Microsoft’s built-in security software for detecting and blocking malware and other threats.
Microsoft Excel product
Microsoft Excel is Microsoft's spreadsheet application for organizing, calculating, and analyzing data.
Microsoft Q&A product
Microsoft's online question-and-answer community for users seeking technical help.
Microsoft Windows product
Microsoft Windows is a widely used operating system for personal computers and servers.
microsoft-365
Microsoft 365 is Microsoft’s cloud productivity and security suite including Office apps, email, storage, and collaboration tools.
microsoft-office product
Microsoft Office is a suite of productivity apps such as Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Outlook.
Military intelligence concept
Military intelligence is the collection and analysis of information to support a country’s armed forces and national security decisions.
Mimikatz tool
Mimikatz is a well-known security tool often used by attackers and defenders to extract passwords and authentication tokens from Windows systems.
Misconfigured concept
Misconfigured means a system or service has been set up incorrectly in a way that can cause security or reliability problems.
missing boundary validation vulnerability
Missing boundary validation means software fails to properly check where data starts or ends, which can let attackers crash it or corrupt memory.
misuse concept
Misuse is using a system, account, or feature in a harmful or unauthorized way.
mitigations concept
Mitigations are steps taken to reduce the chance or impact of a security problem.
ML-DSA-44 protocol
A post-quantum digital-signature algorithm designed to resist attacks from quantum computers.
Model calls concept
Model calls are requests sent to an AI model to get a response or perform a task.
Model-as-Judge Scoring technique
An evaluation method in which an AI model rates the quality, safety, or correctness of another system's output.
model-context-protocol
Model Context Protocol is a standard that lets AI applications connect to external tools, data, and services.
Moderate concept
Moderate usually describes a middle level of risk, severity, or security requirements.
monitoring system concept
A solution that collects and analyzes security-related data in real time to detect anomalies or breaches.
Moral Injury concept
Emotional harm that can result from acting against one's values or being unable to do what one believes is right.
Mouse Personalization Settings product
User-selected Windows settings that control a mouse pointer's appearance and behavior.
Mouse Properties product
A Windows settings panel for changing mouse buttons, pointers, and related options.
Mouse Settings concept
Computer preferences that control how a mouse pointer, buttons, and scrolling behave.
MSI tool
MSI usually refers to Microsoft Installer packages used to install software on Windows.

A phishing technique that sends a visitor through several web redirects, often using trusted-looking domains to hide the final destination.
also: chain of redirects across Google domains
myanmar other
Myanmar is a country in Southeast Asia that may appear in cyber stories as a victim location, actor location, or operating base.
Mythic tool
Mythic is an open-source command-and-control framework used by red teams to manage agents during security testing.
Mythos 5 product
Mythos 5 is a named AI model or model version referenced in reporting.
Nacos authentication bypass vulnerability
A vulnerability that lets an attacker bypass login checks in an affected Nacos server or service.
Namespace concept
A namespace is a named container used to keep identifiers, resources, or settings separate from others so they do not conflict.
Naming Error concept
A mistake in choosing or matching a name, such as confusing a fictional name with a real internet domain.
National Crime Agency organization
The National Crime Agency is a UK law enforcement organization that fights serious and organized crime.
National Cyber Force organization
The National Cyber Force is a United Kingdom military and intelligence organization that conducts offensive cyber operations.
National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency organization
A U.S. intelligence agency that provides maps, imagery, and geographic analysis for national security.
National Security Agency organization
The National Security Agency is a U.S. government agency focused on signals intelligence and cybersecurity.
negotiation concept
Negotiation is the process where two parties or systems agree on terms, settings, or actions before continuing.
NetExec tool
A network-administration and security-testing tool that can run commands and authenticate to remote systems.
Netlas tool
An internet asset search engine used to find publicly exposed systems and services.
NetSupport Manager tool
NetSupport Manager is a legitimate remote administration tool that attackers can also abuse to control a victim's computer.
Network Access concept
Network access means the ability to connect to and use a computer network or resources on it.
network devices product
Network devices are hardware such as routers, switches, firewalls, and access points that move or protect network traffic.
network paths concept
Network paths are routes or addresses used to reach files, systems, or services across a network.
network reconnaissance technique
The initial stage of a cyber attack where attackers scan and map a target network to identify vulnerable systems.
network scanning technique
Network scanning is the process of probing computers or services on a network to find what is reachable and what ports are open.
Network security concept
Network security is the practice of protecting computer networks from unauthorized access, misuse, or attacks.
network traffic concept
Network traffic is the data moving between computers, servers, phones, and other devices over a network.
Nexus tool
Nexus is a named product, tool, or malware family referenced in security reporting, depending on context.
NIST organization
NIST is the U.S. National Institute of Standards and Technology, which creates widely used security standards and guidance.
Node product
Node usually refers to Node.js, a runtime that lets JavaScript run outside a web browser.
Node.js Remote Access Trojan malware
Malware written with Node.js that gives an attacker remote control of an infected device.
noindex Directive concept
An instruction in a web page that asks search engines not to include that page in search results.
Noise concept
Noise is irrelevant or misleading data that makes it harder to notice the important security signals.
Non-English Windows Installations product
Windows systems configured to use a language or regional setting other than English.
noPac technique
A nickname for an attack chain that abuses two Windows Active Directory vulnerabilities to gain powerful domain access.
north-korea other
North Korea is a country often referenced in cybersecurity reports because some hacking groups are alleged to operate on its behalf.
Not Scheduled concept
Not Scheduled is a status label meaning an activity, fix, or event has not yet been assigned a planned date.
npm packages product
npm packages are reusable JavaScript software modules distributed through the npm package ecosystem.
nsa organization
The NSA is a U.S. intelligence agency focused on signals intelligence and protecting certain government communications.

OAuth access is a way for an app to use limited permissions to access an account or service without receiving the user's password.
OAuth Consent Grants protocol
Permissions a user gives an application to access account data or perform actions without sharing the user's password.
obfuscated technique
Obfuscated means code or text has been deliberately made hard to read so people or security tools cannot easily understand what it does.
obfuscated JavaScript technique
Obfuscated JavaScript is JavaScript code intentionally made hard to read so its purpose is harder to understand.
Obfuscated Wrapper technique
Content deliberately made hard to recognize or read so that it can conceal instructions or data.
also: wrapper prompts, crafted prompts, crafted ‘wrapper’ prompt
obfuscation technique
The technique of making code or data deliberately hard to understand to avoid detection by security tools.
offensive cyber concept
Offensive cyber refers to cyber operations intended to disrupt, spy on, or gain access to an adversary's systems.
offensive cyber operations concept
Offensive cyber operations are actions taken to disrupt, access, or gather information from another party’s digital systems.
Office 2016 product
A version of Microsoft's Office productivity software suite.
Office 2019 product
A version of Microsoft's Office productivity software suite.
Office 2024 product
A version of Microsoft's Office productivity software suite.
Office LTSC Standard 2021 product
A long-term supported edition of Microsoft Office intended for organizations that do not use frequent feature updates.
offline monitor tool
A monitoring tool that reviews recorded activity after it happened rather than watching it in real time.
also: The monitor, monitor
Onboarding concept
Onboarding is the process of setting up a new user, employee, device, or service so it can start working safely.
one-time passwords concept
One-time passwords are temporary codes used for a single login or transaction to add an extra layer of security.
online marketplaces concept
Online marketplaces are websites or platforms where buyers and sellers trade goods, services, or digital items.
open internet concept
The open internet means publicly reachable online systems rather than private or restricted networks.
open source concept
Open source means software whose source code is publicly available for people to inspect, use, modify, and share.
open-source project concept
An open-source project is software whose source code is publicly available for people to inspect, use, modify, or contribute to.
Open-source tool tool
An open-source tool is software whose source code is publicly available for people to inspect, use, or modify.
openai organization
OpenAI is an AI company known for ChatGPT and GPT language models.
OpenAI Agents product
Artificial intelligence systems from OpenAI that can perform multi-step tasks using tools or software services.
OpenAI Codex product
OpenAI Codex is an AI coding system designed to understand and generate computer code from natural-language instructions.
OpenAI Responses API protocol
An OpenAI programming interface that lets software send requests to and receive results from AI models.
also: responses API
OpenRouter product
A service that provides access to multiple AI models through a common interface.
Operating system concept
An operating system is the main software that manages a computer or phone, such as Windows, macOS, Android, or iOS.
operating system commands concept
Instructions given to an operating system, like 'dir' on Windows or 'ls' on Linux, to perform actions.
operation-endgame

An Operator is a Kubernetes automation component that manages an application by encoding operational tasks into software.
operators concept
Operators are the people or groups running a system, service, campaign, or criminal operation.
Opus-class models product
Opus-class models are the higher-end Claude AI models designed for more demanding reasoning, writing, coding, and analysis tasks.
Orbit Tracker malware
A malicious browser extension that can collect information from a victim's browser.
order data concept
Order data is information about purchases, such as customer details, items bought, prices, and shipping information.
outbound concept
Outbound traffic is network communication that leaves a device or organization and goes to an outside destination.
OUTPUT action technique
The OUTPUT action is an action in a rule or automation system that sends data out to another destination or component.
Output Monitoring concept
Checking what a system produces or does to detect unsafe, suspicious, or unwanted results.
also: Monitoring the output and actions taken by the LLM, monitoring LLM behavior and output
overlay concept
An overlay is a screen element placed on top of another interface, which can be legitimate or used to trick users.
overlays technique

OVERPASS threat-actor
OVERPASS is a named threat activity or tool referenced in security reporting.
OWASP LLM Top 10 concept

pace concept
Pace is the speed or rhythm of speech, movement, or activity and can be used as a behavior signal.
package registries concept
Package registries are online repositories where developers publish and download reusable software libraries.
package_info.pl tool
package_info.pl is a Perl script name that may be used by software to display or process package information.
Padre product
A cryptocurrency-related online service referenced in security reporting.
Palo Alto Networks organization
A leading global cybersecurity company known for next-generation firewalls and advanced cloud security.

PaperCut NG/MF product
Print-management software used by organizations to manage printers, users, and printing costs.
PaperCut servers product
PaperCut servers are systems running PaperCut print-management software, which organizations use to manage printing and copying.
Paraphrasing concept
Rewriting text in different words while keeping its original meaning.
also: paraphrase, rewrite the prompt in its own terms

Pass-the-hash is an attack technique where someone logs in using a stolen password hash instead of needing the actual password.
passport concept
A passport is an official identity and travel document that may be sensitive if stolen or exposed.
password reset concept
The process of changing a user's password, typically after they've forgotten it or it's been compromised.
password resets concept
The process of changing or recovering a password, often used when a user forgets their current password.
Patch Tuesday concept
Patch Tuesday is Microsoft's regular monthly release day for security updates, usually the second Tuesday of each month.
patched concept
Patched means a software flaw has been fixed with an update.
patches concept
Patches are software updates that fix bugs, security flaws, or other problems.
patching concept
Applying software updates to fix security holes and bugs.
payload concept
A payload is the part of malicious code that performs the attacker’s intended action.
also: embedded payload, original embedded payloads, embedded payload instructions
payloads concept
Payloads are the parts of malware or an exploit that perform the attacker's intended action, such as stealing data or installing ransomware.
payment card details concept
Credit or debit card information such as the number, expiration date, and CVV, highly sought by criminals for fraud.
Payment card information concept
Payment card information is data from credit or debit cards, such as card numbers, names, expiration dates, or security codes.
Payment details concept
Payment details are information used to pay for something, such as card numbers, billing addresses, or bank account data.
Payment fraud concept
Payment fraud is the unauthorized or deceptive use of payment methods to steal money or goods.
payment methods concept
Payment methods are ways people pay for goods or services, such as cards, bank transfers, or cryptocurrency.

Payment processing is the system that handles card, bank, or digital payments between buyers and sellers.
Payment systems concept
Payment systems are the services and networks that let people and businesses send, receive, and process money.
Pentagon organization
The Pentagon is the headquarters of the U.S. Department of Defense and is often used to refer to that department.
perimeter concept
A perimeter is the boundary between an organization's internal network and outside networks such as the internet.
Permission Middleware tool
Software that checks whether an action is authorized before allowing a tool or service request to proceed.
also: permission checks, authorization at the tool boundary
Permission to Draw Over Other Apps concept
An Android permission that lets an app display content on top of other apps.
persistence concept
Persistence is the ability for an attacker to keep access to a system over time.
persistent access concept
Persistent access means continued access to an account or system over time.
Persistent remote access technique
Persistent remote access means an attacker keeps a way to reconnect to a system even after reboots or temporary disruptions.
personal information concept
Personal information is data that can identify or describe a person, such as a name, address, phone number, or account details.
Personal Space concept
The normal personal area of an Android phone outside its separate work profile.
philippines other
The Philippines is a country in Southeast Asia that may be mentioned in cyber reports as a victim location, actor location, or operating base.
phishing technique
Phishing is a scam where attackers impersonate trusted people or services to steal information or make victims take unsafe actions.
phishing campaign technique
A phishing campaign is a coordinated effort to trick people into giving up passwords, money, or other sensitive information.
phishing campaigns technique
Phishing campaigns are organized attempts to trick many people into revealing information or installing malware using fake messages.
phishing email technique
A phishing email is a fake or deceptive message designed to trick someone into revealing information or clicking something harmful.
phishing emails technique
Phishing emails are fake messages designed to trick people into revealing information or clicking harmful links.
phishing messages technique
Phishing messages are fake emails, texts, or chats that try to trick people into giving up information or clicking something dangerous.
phishing pages technique
Phishing pages are fake web pages designed to trick people into entering passwords, codes, or other sensitive information.
phishing-as-a-service concept

phone numbers concept

physical damage concept

pig-butchering technique

Pilot Programs concept
Small trial projects used to test an idea or technology before wider deployment.
pinned concept
Pinned means fixed to a specific version, commit, certificate, or value so it does not change unexpectedly.

A fixed comparison point used to detect whether later software or model results have become worse.

A pipeline is an automated sequence of steps used to build, test, or deploy software.

Plain Prose concept
Ordinary natural writing that is not encoded, encrypted, or formatted as code.
also: plain English, ordinary-looking prose
Platform data concept
Platform data is information collected or stored by an online service about users, content, activity, or transactions.

Play Protect is Google's Android security service that scans apps and devices for harmful behavior.

A name used for security research into attack paths involving Windows Plug and Play automatic installation.

A feature that lets a computer recognize connected hardware and automatically set it up for use.

Polygon blockchain product

Port scanning is checking a computer or network to see which network services are reachable.
post-exploitation technique
Post-exploitation is what attackers do after breaking in, such as exploring systems, stealing data, or keeping access.
post-quantum algorithm concept
Encryption methods designed to remain secure even against the future powerful attacks of quantum computers.
post-quantum algorithms protocol
Post-quantum algorithms are cryptographic methods designed to resist attacks from quantum computers.
powershell

Pre-authentication means something happens before a user has logged in or proven who they are.

Pre-authentication remote code execution is a serious flaw that lets an attacker run code on a system from afar without needing to log in first.
Precise concept
Carefully targeted and intended to avoid unnecessary effects.
Preferences concept
Preferences is a browser settings file or area where user options and configuration values are stored.

Previdian is a named organization, product, or service referenced in security reporting.

An optional software update released for testing or early access before its normal wider release.

private data concept
Sensitive information that should not be publicly disclosed, like personal identifiers or financial records.

Private information is personal or confidential data that should not be shared without permission.
private key concept

privilege-escalation technique

production systems concept
Production systems are the real live systems an organization uses to run its services or business.

The live servers and network systems used to provide a VPN service to customers.

Security protections used on live systems that handle real users or business operations.

prompts concept
Prompts are the instructions or questions a user gives to an AI system to get a response.

Proofpoint is a cybersecurity company known for email security, threat intelligence, and data protection products.
Prophet Security organization
Prophet Security is a cybersecurity company or product name referenced in security reporting.

Provenance means the origin and history of something, such as where software came from and how it was built.

A security tool referenced in reporting about ransomware attacks.
PSSpoof tool
A security tool referenced in reporting about ransomware attacks.

The public internet is the globally accessible network that anyone can connect to through internet service providers.
also: real internet, real systems, real-world systems, live public host

Publicly disclosed means information has been made available for the public to know.

quantum computers concept
